Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "we need a prompt for the next inventory check at cedar lane food cooperative, using the notes below. The request is to prepare draft reorder quantities for the six listed stock items, but only if the check condition is satisfied. Please make that the main task, not something to do regardless. The count sheet is dated May 18, and the records to check are the inventory ledger plus every receiving slip for deliveries through May 17. The condition is that, for all six items, the physical count agrees with the ledger and each receiving slip through May 17 is accounted for in the ledger. A slip that is missing, unsigned, or not clearly posted means the condition has not been shown to hold. If it does not hold, the useful alternative is a discrepancy list that identifies the item and the specific record or count needing verification. In that case, do not calculate or show reorder quantities.

We have six lines, all quantities are in the selling unit named for the item. brown rice, 25-pound bag: physical count 18 bags; ledger balance 18; target level 30; open purchase order 6. chickpeas, 10-pound bag: physical count 11 bags; ledger balance 12; target level 20; open purchase order 0. oats, 20-pound sack: physical count 9 sacks; ledger balance 9; target level 18; open purchase order 4. canned tomatoes, case of 12 cans: physical count 24 cases; ledger balance 24; target level 36; open purchase order 12. olive oil, 1-liter bottle: physical count 7 bottles; ledger balance 7; target level 16; open purchase order 4. apple sauce, case of 12 jars: physical count 14 cases; ledger balance 14; target level 24; open purchase order 6. Don't change units or combine items. These are the notes from the board and the count sheet, not an instruction to assume that they reconcile with the source documents.

For the document check, the receiving-slip register says brown rice had no delivery through May 17. The chickpea delivery slip dated May 16 says 5 bags received; the ledger entry for May 16 records 4 bags. For oats, the May 17 slip says 8 sacks received, and the ledger has an 8-sack entry dated May 17. The physical count sheet says the count was taken after the receiving window closed, but the notes don't say whether the delivery was put away before the count. The canned-tomato slip dated May 17 says 12 cases received and the ledger has a 12-case entry on that date. The olive-oil register lists a May 17 delivery of 3 cases, but the slip in the file has no receiver signature; the ledger has a 36-bottle entry dated May 17. The apple-sauce slip dated May 15 says 10 cases received, and the ledger has a 10-case entry dated May 15. The notes don't explain the olive-oil case pack, so don't convert its receipt into bottles unless the source records establish the unit. Retain that point as a verification issue if needed.

If and only if the condition holds for every item, calculate draft reorder quantities using this rule: target level minus the verified physical count minus the open purchase order, with a minimum of zero. The target level and open purchase order figures above are already stated in each item's selling unit. Treat the open purchase orders as stock that will arrive, and do not add an extra buffer or round to a different pack size. Label the result as a draft. Do not quietly substitute ledger balances for physical counts or resolve any record conflict by guessing. If the condition fails for even one line, take the alternative path for the inventory check rather than giving partial reorder figures for the apparently clean lines.

The store coordinator said, “we can use the dock tally if the signed slips are still in the blue folder.” The dock tally is not included in these notes, and that remark does not establish that the missing signature has been resolved. Don't claim to have reviewed a folder or another record that isn't supplied. Keep the quoted wording as a note, not as a rule that overrides the condition. Make the prompt ask for verification only from the information provided, and identify any additional record needed without pretending it is available.

Please organize the next prompt so the conditional decision is easy to follow. A numbered section for the decision steps would be useful: first check the condition across all six items; next take exactly one path, either prepare the draft reorder table or produce the discrepancy list. For the reorder path, include item, verified physical count, target level, open purchase order, and draft quantity. For the fallback, include item, discrepancy or missing evidence, and what needs verification. Don't mix the two outputs. Keep all supplied dates and quantities, and make clear that the figures are from the notes rather than independently verified.

The output from the inventory check should contain only the applicable table or discrepancy list, with no introduction, closing paragraph, or general inventory advice. If the condition fails, the list should be useful to the person checking the ledger and receiving file, but it should not turn into a reorder recommendation. The cooperative is preparing the next stock review from this specific May count; the prompt should not ask for pricing, suppliers, substitutions, ordering approval, or an explanation of what the cooperative should do after verification. Keep the final request focused on this inventory check and its one conditional fallback.", "output": "Create a prompt for an inventory check at Cedar Lane Food Cooperative using the notes below. The primary task is to prepare draft reorder quantities for all six listed stock items, but only if the stated condition is satisfied. Otherwise, use the fallback described below. Do not perform the inventory check in this prompt.

### Inventory notes
The count sheet is dated May 18. The figures below are from the board and count sheet and have not been independently verified. Quantities are in each item’s stated selling unit.

| Item | Physical count | Ledger balance | Target level | Open purchase order |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Brown rice, 25-pound bag | 18 bags | 18 | 30 | 6 |
| Chickpeas, 10-pound bag | 11 bags | 12 | 20 | 0 |
| Oats, 20-pound sack | 9 sacks | 9 | 18 | 4 |
| Canned tomatoes, case of 12 cans | 24 cases | 24 | 36 | 12 |
| Olive oil, 1-liter bottle | 7 bottles | 7 | 16 | 4 |
| Apple sauce, case of 12 jars | 14 cases | 14 | 24 | 6 |

Do not change units or combine items.

### Receiving records noted
- Brown rice: The register shows no delivery through May 17.
- Chickpeas: The May 16 receiving slip says 5 bags were received; the ledger records 4 bags on May 16.
- Oats: The May 17 slip says 8 sacks were received, and the ledger has an 8-sack entry dated May 17. The count sheet says the physical count was taken after the receiving window closed, but does not say whether the delivery was put away before the count.
- Canned tomatoes: The May 17 slip says 12 cases were received, and the ledger has a 12-case entry dated May 17.
- Olive oil: The register lists a May 17 delivery of 3 cases, but the slip on file has no receiver signature. The ledger has a 36-bottle entry dated May 17. The notes do not establish the case pack, so do not convert cases to bottles unless the source records establish the unit; flag this for verification if needed.
- Apple sauce: The May 15 slip says 10 cases were received, and the ledger has a 10-case entry dated May 15.

The store coordinator said, “we can use the dock tally if the signed slips are still in the blue folder.” The dock tally is not included, and this remark does not establish that the missing signature has been resolved. Do not claim to have reviewed the folder or any other record that was not supplied. Treat the quote as a note, not as a rule overriding the condition. Identify additional records needed without implying they are available.

### 1. Check the condition and choose one path
The condition holds only if, for all six items, the May 18 physical count agrees with the ledger and every receiving slip for a delivery through May 17 is accounted for in the ledger. A slip that is missing, unsigned, or not clearly posted means the condition has not been shown to hold. Check this condition across all six items before producing an output.

If and only if the condition holds for every item, calculate a draft reorder quantity for each item as: target level minus verified physical count minus open purchase order, with a minimum of zero. Treat open purchase orders as stock that will arrive. Do not add a buffer or round to a different pack size. Label the quantities as drafts. Do not replace physical counts with ledger balances or resolve conflicts by guessing.

If the condition fails for even one item, do not calculate or show any reorder quantities, including for lines that appear to reconcile. Instead, produce a useful discrepancy list identifying each item and the specific count, record, or missing evidence needing verification. The fallback must not become a reorder recommendation.

### Output requirements
Return only the applicable output, with no introduction, closing paragraph, or general inventory advice. For the reorder path, provide a table with item, verified physical count, target level, open purchase order, and draft quantity. For the fallback, provide a list with item, discrepancy or missing evidence, and what needs verification. Keep the two outputs separate and include all supplied dates and quantities where relevant. Focus only on this May inventory check; do not ask for pricing, suppliers, substitutions, ordering approval, or advice about what to do after verification."}]
